title: What is a length-4 rod worth?
hook: Sell it whole for $9, or cut it into pieces first. Which pays, and how much?

knows: smaller answers combine into bigger ones (ways-to-make-ten)
doesNotKnow: that the best price of a rod asks for the best price of every shorter rod

misconception: The most money comes from selling the rod whole, or cutting off the best-priced piece once.
objective: The learner can explain that the best price of a rod is the largest, over every first-piece length, of that piece's price plus the best price of the rest, so with prices $1, $5, $8, $9 the length-4 rod is worth $10 as 2 + 2, more than $9 whole.

claims.text: Prices: a piece of length 1 sells for $1, length 2 for $5, length 3 for $8, and length 4 (the whole rod) for $9.
claims.source: The lesson's price list (PRICE in Demo.tsx), the first four prices of the CLRS rod-cutting example (CLRS 4e section 14.1, Figure 14.1; 3e section 15.1, Figure 15.1). · Fact-check pass 21 2026-10-14: VERIFIED: Demo PRICE = [1,5,8,9], shown in the predict stem and stage note. CLRS Figure 14.1 prices from memory (1 5 8 9 10 17 17 20 24 30), not opened; the prices are a lesson convention either way.

claims.text: With these prices, best(1) to best(4) are $1, $5, $8, $10; the length-4 rod's best is two pieces of length 2 ($5 + $5 = $10), which beats selling it whole ($9) and cutting off the most expensive piece, length 3, and selling the leftover ($8 + $1 = $9).
claims.source: Demo.tsx solve() (the recurrence below) gives 1, 5, 8, 10 with best cut 2 + 2. Builder's node script (2026-10-14) enumerated all 8 ordered cuttings of length 4: 4, 7, 7, 9, 7, 10, 9, 9; only 2 + 2 reaches 10. · Fact-check pass 21 2026-10-14: VERIFIED: node rod.mjs, Demo solve(): 1 5 8 10, cut 2+2. Own enumeration of the 8 ordered cuttings of 4: 4 7 7 9 7 10 9 9; only 2+2 = 10. · v3 (2026-10-14): 'best-priced' reworded to 'most expensive' (learner r7 finding 4). | FC pass 26 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own node port of solve(): best(1..4) = 1, 5, 8, 10, pieces 2+2; brute force over all cuttings agrees; length-4 cut list reads 1+best(3) $9, 2+best(2) $10, 3+best(1) $9 (= $8 + $1), whole $9. Length 3 ($8) is the most expensive of the cut pieces offered ($1, $5, $8). Reveal values are constants of the table, true after Start over too.

claims.text: The best price of a rod is the largest, over every first-piece length, of that piece's price plus the best price of the rest (stage: 'best(n) = largest of: piece + best(rest)'; the choice list shows each cut as 'k + best(n - k): price(k) + best(n - k) = total', or 'whole n' for no cut).
claims.source: CLRS 4e section 14.1, recurrence r(n) = max over 1 <= i <= n of (p(i) + r(n - i)), with r(0) = 0; it relies on optimal substructure (the rest of an optimal cutting is itself cut optimally), same section. · Fact-check pass 21 2026-10-14: VERIFIED: Derivation: every cutting has some first piece k, and the rest is a cutting of n-k worth at most best(n-k), achieved by its best cutting; so best(n) = max_k p(k) + best(n-k). Matches Demo solve() and the choice list. CLRS 14.1 from memory, not opened. · v3 (2026-10-14): cut-line wording changed to name the reused row, best(n - k); re-check needed. | FC pass 26 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED on derivation (CLRS not opened): every cutting has a first piece k, and the rest is worth at most best(n-k), reached by its best cutting, so best(n) = max_k price(k) + best(n-k). Stage strings re-generated in node: note "best(n) = largest of: first piece + best of the rest"; lines "k + best(n - k): $p + $r = $t" and "whole n: $p + $0 = $p". | v4 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14): learner r8 phone fit: the stage rule line is shortened to 'best(n) = largest of: piece + best(rest)' (one line on a phone); reveal sentence unchanged. Needs re-check. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Verified by derivation and enumeration; CLRS was not opened. Proof: any cutting of n has some first piece k, and its rest must itself be cut at its best (otherwise swapping in a better cut of the rest raises the total), so best(n) = max over k of price(k) + best(n − k), with best(0) = 0. Own brute force over every composition matches the recurrence for this price list (1, 5, 8, 10) and for 2,000 random price lists of length 1 to 9 (0 mismatches). Stage text: 'best(n) = largest of: piece + best(rest)'. The list renders 'k + best(n−k): $p + $r = $t' and 'whole n: $p + $0 = $p' (own render of n = 1..4).

claims.text: Each cut line read a filled row, like best(2) in '2 + best(2)' (the outlined row): each shorter rod is solved once and reused (stage: the row the kept cut reuses is outlined).
claims.source: Bottom-up order in Demo.tsx: best(n) reads only best(0..n-1), which are already in the table, so each length is computed once (n lengths, at most n choices each: O(n^2) work). CLRS 4e section 14.1, BOTTOM-UP-CUT-ROD. · Fact-check pass 21 2026-10-14: VERIFIED: Demo TABLE = solve(PRICE) computed once; choices(n) reads TABLE[n-k] for k = 1..n, all already filled because the learner fills in order. · v3 (2026-10-14): reveal sentence reworded; stage now outlines the row n - first for the kept cut (row 2 at length 4). | FC pass 26 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Rows fill in order (Fill / Fill the rest), so every "k + best(m)" line at length n reads a row m < n that is already filled; TABLE is computed once. Outline: reused = n - first only when the kept cut is not whole, which is row 2 at length 4 (lengths 1-3 keep the whole piece, no outline). "1 + best(3)" is the first line of the length-4 list, on stage at best-4 (needed for the reveal); after Start over the reveal's past tense holds. | v4 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14): learner r8: the reveal's example was best(3) in '1 + best(3)', but the dashed outline is on the row the kept cut reads (row 2 at best(4)); the example now names that row: best(2) in '2 + best(2)' (the outlined row). Needs re-check. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. In Demo.tsx, choices(n) reads TABLE[n − k].best for k = 1..n, and the list shows only n = filled, so every row it reads (length < n) is filled. The outlined row is reused = n − TABLE[n].first: for n = 4 the kept cut is k = 2 (first strict max), so row 2 is outlined, matching the reveal's 'best(2) in "2 + best(2)"'. SyncOnReveal refills to 4 when the reveal opens after best(4) was seen, so the outlined row is on stage even if Start over was pressed last.

claims.text: With prices 1, 5, 8, 9, 10, 17, 17, 20 for lengths 1 to 8, a length-8 rod sells for $22 (pieces 2 + 6), not $20 whole.

recall.question: You know the best price for every rod shorter than 5. How do you find the best price for a rod of length 5?
options: For each first piece, add its price to the best price of what is left, and keep the largest
Compare selling it whole with cutting off the most expensive piece
List every way to cut it and price each one from scratch
recall.why: The rest of a best cutting is itself cut the best way, so the best for 5 is the largest of price(k) + best(5 - k). The shorter answers are already known, so nothing is recomputed.
